statusDetail: Coverage-complete representative audit of five public templates/journeys. Not covered: authenticated account internals, completed payment, personalized logged-in states, live search submission, and real offline transport because they require credentials, financial commitment, or broader destructive/environmental controls.

page.notes: Large server-rendered Argentine news MPA/hybrid. Raw HTML contains 91% of rendered content. All sampled pages show a first-load consent wall.

checkOutcomes.method: Computed-style probes under explicit prefers-color-scheme conditions.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Under explicit light and dark emulation the body changes from transparent/light to rgb(33,33,33); the site also exposes a day/night mode.
With prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the probe found no active animations or autoplay media.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse contrast audit plus prefers-contrast screenshot.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse found three contrast failures, including 1.82:1 in the consent control; no high-contrast adaptation was visible.

checkOutcomes.method: Route/template screenshots and rendered DOM review.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Representative MPA route changes showed no observed transition animation.
No scroll-linked visual effect was present on sampled templates, so no main-thread scroll-animation anti-pattern affected the experience.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM and visual inspection across homepage and subscription surfaces.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Primary interactions use native links, scrolling, checkboxes and buttons; no gesture surface that fights platform scrolling was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Computed header style and layout metrics.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The primary header is position:static on a 17,149px feed and no progress/state cue was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Overlay DOM and screenshots at desktop/mobile viewport edges.
checkOutcomes.evidence: The sampled overlays are centered modal surfaces rather than edge-attached tooltips/popovers; no drifting anchored UI was observed.

checkOutcomes.method: Visual review of section/article and error recovery templates.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Section labels, story hierarchy and the 404 recovery page visibly direct users to relevant next destinations.

checkOutcomes.method: First-load screenshots across all representative templates.
checkOutcomes.evidence: A blocking consent modal obscures every sampled primary page on first load.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM primitive and semantic element probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Probe found four role=dialog containers, one dialog and no popovers; visible consent UI is custom modal chrome.
Multiple stacked promo/navigation bands plus the blocking CMP dominate the first viewport.
At 360x800, scrollWidth equals clientWidth (360px), horizontal overflow is 0 and viewport meta is present.

checkOutcomes.method: Computed-style DOM inspection at sampled core containers.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Sampled core containers report container-type:normal; no component-level container adaptation was evidenced.
Focused menu control has no outline/box-shadow and 110 rendered targets are under 24px in one dimension.
The editorial purpose is clear behind the page, but a first-load consent wall hides it on all core paths.
Homepage links lead to a readable article and section; subscription offers expose prices and subscribe actions without a dead end in the sampled pre-purchase flow.
The missing route explains that content is unavailable and offers portada, latest-news, dollar, games and horoscope recovery links.
Lighthouse: LCP 7.0s, TBT 2,110ms, performance 28; independent trace LCP 8.79s.
Measured CLS is 0.078 in Lighthouse, 0.082 mobile and 0.013 desktop, all below the 0.1 good threshold.
Lighthouse TBT is 2,110ms; trace records five long tasks up to 118ms.

checkOutcomes.method: HAR summary confirmed against live script attributes.
checkOutcomes.evidence: 557 requests transfer 13.44MB and a parser-inserted zonda script is neither async nor defer.
Lighthouse estimates 1,674KiB unused JS and 61KiB unused CSS.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse accessibility audits and DOM probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse fails link-name; probe finds eight unlabelled controls and 70 empty unnamed links.
Lighthouse finds three insufficient-contrast nodes, including a 1.82:1 consent label.
No main landmark exists; consent markup adds multiple H1s; keyboard focus is visually absent on the menu control.
Article headline, deck and listing copy render at readable sizes with clear typographic hierarchy in sampled desktop/mobile screenshots.
Viewport permits user scaling and mobile reflow has no overflow, but 110 interactive targets are below 24px in one dimension.
Lighthouse records seven console/network errors including CORS, FedCM and JW Player failures.

checkOutcomes.method: DOM metadata, image primitive and Lighthouse.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Doctype and UTF-8 are valid, but image audit finds 9 missing dimensions and broad sizing/format inefficiency.
Lighthouse detects notification permission requested on load and a BFCache failure.
Homepage and article have unique descriptive titles and meta descriptions.
All 1,038 sampled anchors have hrefs, viewport metadata is present, robots permits indexing and raw content is available.
Homepage and article expose matching canonicals; robots says all/max-image-preview and sitemap/robots endpoints respond with indexing directives.
Homepage has six JSON-LD blocks and seven Open Graph tags; article has five JSON-LD blocks and complete article OG title/description/image/url metadata.
HTTPS is used, but all six inspected security header families are absent and many cookies lack Secure.

checkOutcomes.method: Tracker and HAR summaries plus consent vendor list.
checkOutcomes.evidence: 63 third-party origins, 16 known trackers, 355 third-party requests and 6.61MB third-party transfer occur on first load.

checkOutcomes.method: Lighthouse permission audit and public-flow review.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Lighthouse detected a notification prompt on load, which is not contextual; account entry exists but modern auth could not be verified before sign-in.
HSTS, clickjacking protection, CSP, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy are all absent.
Raw HTML contains 91% of rendered content words, including title/H1/description; crawler view is substantive, not a JS shell.

checkOutcomes.method: Responsive overlay screenshots and error-state probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Sampled centered overlays remain within desktop/mobile viewports and missing-route navigation remains usable.

checkOutcomes.method: Contextual applicability judgement from recon; service-worker capability exists but no manifest URL was exposed.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Clarín is primarily a public news/content MPA rather than an installed app; offline installability was not treated as a required core task.
checkOutcomes.reason: Offline/installable behavior is contextual and not required for this representative public-news reading scope.

checkOutcomes.method: Deliberate missing-route screenshot and DOM probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: A missing URL renders a complete, explanatory recovery page with multiple useful destinations instead of a blank shell.
The document declares lang=es and Spanish reading order is correct on all sampled templates.
Visible dates and Argentine subscription prices are formatted in Spanish/Argentine conventions, e.g. “sábado, 18 de julio de 2026” and $1.978.
The sampled public pages expose publication/calendar text but no user-scheduled or cross-time-zone transaction to validate.
checkOutcomes.reason: No representative time-zone-sensitive user flow exists in the sampled public news and subscription surfaces.

checkOutcomes.evidence: The CMP is intrusive, but accept and reject are both explicit, similarly styled actions; subscription cards disclose introductory and later monthly prices plus cancellation copy.
Required-field messages are English on a Spanish page and invalid controls lack aria-invalid/aria-describedby.
Personal-data fields in the subscription form omit autocomplete tokens.
Subscription offers show promotional and subsequent monthly prices, “Cancelá cuando quieras. Sin cargos”, login and telephone options before commitment.
Image audit reports 91 non-lazy below-fold, 79 without srcset, 94 legacy-format and 37 oversized images.
First load performs 557 requests including 163 XHR/fetch and remains interactive only after 74.6s.
Third parties account for 355 requests and 6.61MB; player imagery and scripts are among the top byte offenders.
The public news site exposes crawlable SSR content but no declared agent transaction/tool surface requiring WebMCP.
checkOutcomes.reason: Emerging structured agent capabilities were judged out of scope for a read-only public news surface.

checkOutcomes.evidence: No user-facing on-device summarization or language-model feature is part of the sampled core news/subscription journeys.
checkOutcomes.reason: On-device inference is contextual and no such product intent or surface was observed.

checkOutcomes.evidence: After ten full-feed bottom/top cycles, heap self-size changed only +6,997 bytes and entry count +1,395 between comparable isolated captures; major object/closure populations did not grow.

checkOutcomes.method: Heap summary and rendered-DOM size probe.
checkOutcomes.evidence: Baseline heap summary is 144,877,541 self-size bytes across 2,452,687 entries, disproportionate for a news listing.
No Detached* constructor appears among summarized dominant constructors, and closures decline from 166,932 to 165,782 after repeated scrolling.

principleOutcomes.reason: Emerging structured agent capabilities were judged out of scope for a read-only public news surface. On-device inference is contextual and no such product intent or surface was observed.

paths.description: Homepage and news-feed template; entry point, navigation, consent, performance and responsive behavior.
Politics section listing; representative section/index template.
Current politics article; representative article/detail and reading journey.
Subscription offer and contact form; representative commercial/form journey.
Deliberately missing route; representative HTTP/error recovery state.

findings.summary: A consent wall obscures every sampled content and commercial page on first load.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show an opaque modal and dimmed page covering the primary news, article, section and subscription content before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the blocking first-load wall with the least intrusive consent surface permitted, preserve an equally prominent reject action, and defer non-essential vendors until a choice is made.

findings.summary: Some text and controls fail minimum contrast, including inside the consent UI.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility reports three contrast failures; “Más información” is measured at 1.82:1 where 4.5:1 is required. The prefers-contrast screenshot shows no compensating treatment.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic color tokens with WCAG-compliant contrast and add forced-colors/prefers-contrast adaptations for essential controls.

findings.summary: Full-page route changes do not expose a view-transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The sampled site is a Next.js MPA/hybrid; route screenshots and DOM evidence show conventional abrupt document swaps and no observed transition animation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add same-origin cross-document View Transitions with a reduced-motion-safe fallback for section/article navigation.

findings.summary: The primary header is static rather than scroll-state aware.
findings.evidence: DOM computed evidence reports header position: static on a feed over 17,000 CSS px tall; no scroll progress or shrinking state was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sticky chrome sparingly and expose scroll state/progress with CSS scroll-state queries or a lightweight progress indicator.

findings.summary: Modal UI relies predominantly on custom role=dialog containers.
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found four [role=dialog] elements but only one dialog element and no popover elements; the visible CMP is a custom modal surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Prefer native dialog/popover primitives with platform focus management and light-dismiss semantics where the interaction allows.

findings.summary: The first viewport is crowded with promos, live-topic bars and ad/consent chrome.
findings.evidence: The desktop screenshot shows multiple stacked navigation/promo strips before story content, then a full blocking CMP; the page loads 557 resources around a content feed.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate header bands, reserve the first viewport for editorial hierarchy, and load secondary promotional chrome after core content.

findings.summary: Core sampled containers do not expose component-level responsiveness.
findings.evidence: DOM computed styles report container-type: normal for the sampled header and other primary structures; adaptation appears viewport-driven.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reusable story cards and navigation modules that appear at multiple widths.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch-target support are incomplete.
findings.evidence: The focused side-menu checkbox has outline:none and no box shadow; the probe counts 110 rendered interactive targets below 24 px in at least one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a strong :focus-visible treatment and enlarge interactive hit areas to at least 24x24 CSS px, preferably 44x44 for primary controls.

findings.summary: Cold-load performance is poor.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse performance is 28 with FCP 5.2s, LCP 7.0s, TBT 2,110ms, Speed Index 22.8s and interactive at 74.6s; the independent trace measured LCP 8.79s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reduce initial JavaScript and third parties, and schedule non-critical work after the core news content is usable.

findings.summary: Heavy scripting blocks the main thread.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured 2,110ms TBT. The trace recorded five long tasks, up to 118ms, while the layout observer saw repeated long tasks.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up long tasks, defer ad/player initialization, and conditionally load scripts only when their surface approaches the viewport.

findings.summary: The homepage network dependency graph is extremely large.
findings.evidence: HAR records 557 requests and 13.44MB transferred. A parser-inserted zonda script in the head is neither async nor defer; the trace LCP is 8.79s.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove parser-blocking scripts from the critical path, conditionally load media/ad stacks, and apply useful caching and priority hints only to true critical resources.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused JavaScript and CSS.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 1,674KiB unused JavaScript and 61KiB unused CSS; the 1.16MB Next.js app chunk alone wastes about 262KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by route and feature, remove duplicated analytics tags, and load player/ad/auth code only when needed.

findings.summary: Some interactive controls lack usable accessible names or labels.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails link-name; the DOM probe finds eight unlabelled controls and 70 links with no text, aria-label or labelled image in the sampled rendered DOM.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every actionable link/control a stable accessible name and associate labels with all non-hidden form fields.

findings.summary: Landmark and heading structure is polluted by consent markup.
findings.evidence: The homepage has no main landmark. The rendered H1 set includes the Clarín masthead plus CMP headings; the article likewise exposes its article title and multiple CMP H1s.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one main landmark around primary content, keep one page-level H1, and use lower-level headings inside the consent component while preserving its accessible dialog label.

findings.summary: The page logs multiple runtime and network errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse lists seven console/network errors, including CORS failures, a failed JW Player placement and a FedCM token failure.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove or guard failing integrations, correct CORS configuration, and do not initialize media/auth components when prerequisites are unavailable.

findings.summary: Image delivery is wasteful across the long news feed.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 91 below-fold images without lazy loading, 79 without srcset, 94 legacy-format images and 37 oversized images; HAR attributes 7.44MB to images.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold images, emit responsive srcset/sizes, negotiate AVIF/WebP, and request dimensions close to rendered card size.

findings.summary: The page requests notification permission on load and is not BFCache eligible.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails notification-on-start and reports a BFCache failure; unsolicited permission prompts are not user-initiated.
findings.suggestedFix: Request notifications only after an explicit user action and remove avoidable BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: Baseline browser security policies and cookie flags are missing.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence finds no CSP, HSTS, nosniff, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence reports 20 cookies without Secure among the sampled set and widespread SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP with frame-ancestors, HSTS, nosniff, strict Referrer/Permissions policies, and set Secure plus the narrowest suitable SameSite on every cookie.

findings.summary: The anonymous first load has an outsized third-party tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence sees 63 third-party origins and 16 known trackers. HAR records 355 third-party requests and 6.61MB third-party transfer while the CMP names 237 partners.
findings.suggestedFix: Block non-essential vendors until consent, reduce vendor count, consolidate analytics, shorten identifier lifetimes and publish a defensible data-minimisation budget.

findings.summary: The Spanish subscription form falls back to unconnected English browser error messages.
findings.evidence: Empty required fields return English validationMessage strings such as “Please fill in this field”; invalid controls have no aria-invalid or aria-describedby, although an assertive live region exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate after interaction with localized Spanish messages, set aria-invalid, connect each message with aria-describedby and announce the error summary.

findings.summary: The subscription contact form omits autocomplete tokens for personal data.
findings.evidence: Name, surname, email, phone and document fields all expose autocomplete="" in the form probe.
findings.suggestedFix: Add correct autocomplete tokens such as given-name, family-name, email and tel; use an appropriate documented token or policy for national ID.

findings.summary: Background integrations perform disproportionate work before core content settles.
findings.evidence: The first load makes 557 requests, including 163 XHR/fetch requests and large player/ad/analytics stacks; Lighthouse remains interactive only after 74.6s.
findings.suggestedFix: Deprioritize background fetches, batch analytics, stop initializing offscreen media, and gate expensive vendors on visibility and consent.

findings.summary: The homepage has a very large steady-state heap for a news listing.
findings.evidence: Heap summary reports 2,452,687 nodes/heap entries and 144,877,541 self-size bytes, including 166,932 closures; the rendered DOM is also about 5.9MB.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce mounted feed/ad/player trees, release dormant integration state, virtualize or progressively render long lists, and profile allocation retainers for the largest native/object populations.
findings.guidanceId: bounded memory footprint javascript heap size page weight proportionate allocations
